concerns.message: The player count comes from the synced ships map. `hud.ts:25` renders `model.ships.length`, `HeadlessClient.playerCount` returns `state.ships.size`, and `scripts/smoke-build.ts:111` plus the admission and match integration tests wait for `playerCount === 2/4/8`. Once StateView filters ships, that number becomes "ships I can see". The skeleton's spawn slots are about 20 tiles apart and the planned sight radius is about 10 tiles, so each client sees only itself. The plan never says where the true player count comes from.
concerns.consequence: The integration tests that wait for 4 or 8 players time out. Worse, the HUD shows '1' in a two-player match with the ships out of sight, and no browser scenario catches it: join-private-match checks only one player. The quick fixes are either a wrong HUD or a public per-player record that carries slot or position and leaks it. Add a public count-only field (for example `playerCount` on MatchState) and point the HUD, HeadlessClient and smoke build at it.

concerns.message: The drift test cannot live in `packages/content/src`. `tests/unit/purity.test.ts` bans `fs` imports in the pure packages and scans `.test.ts` files too, and the content tsconfig has `types: []`, so there are no Node types. `tests/unit` is not an owned path. The only unit-test location that is both in bounds and in the unit project is `apps/*/src/**/*.test.ts`.
concerns.consequence: A worker who writes `packages/content/src/map.test.ts` with `readFileSync` fails purity and typecheck. They may then report `blocked` under the 'needs a path outside owned paths' stop rule. Tell them up front: put the converter's core in content as a pure function (parsed tmj object → module text), keep a thin fs wrapper in `scripts/`, and put the drift test in e.g. `apps/server/src/seaMap.test.ts`, which reads the .tmj, runs the pure converter and compares against the generated file.

concerns.message: The example placement setting ("an environment variable read by the dev and test entry points") is global to the server process. But `tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts` starts one server for all four scenarios, and they need different layouts: two ships in sight (two-ships-sync), two ships out of sight (out-of-sight), and one ship near a shoal and dock (sail-and-dock). Also, `createMatchOptionsSchema` is a non-strict `z.object`, which silently strips unknown keys, so an extra create option quietly disappears unless the schema is changed.
concerns.consequence: A static spawn list set by an env var can't satisfy all three scenarios, which means rework mid-run. The likely workarounds are hacks such as starting two ships in sight and sailing one away. Better: the env var only unlocks a per-match placement request, such as a gated debug message or an optional layout field that the server ignores unless the flag is set. It never touches admission, and it gets its own test showing it is inert by default.

concerns.message: The travel-time targets set the map's scale, and the plan leaves that open. At the skeleton's 5 tiles/s, neighbouring islands 20–40 s apart means 100–200 tiles of sea between them, so the map is roughly 250×250 tiles, or more than 60k cells. A map that size can't realistically be hand-authored as a .tmj, becomes a huge literal module, and gets drawn tile by tile in Phaser.
concerns.consequence: If max speed and tile scale are not fixed first, the worker gets pushed around by the validator: they re-tune the map, the speed or both several times, the generated module bloats typecheck (keep it as annotated string rows, never a huge `as const` tuple), and drawing one Graphics rect per tile makes the browser tests slow or flaky. Set max speed at about 2–3 tiles/s so the map stays near 100×80 tiles, and draw the terrain once into a texture.

concerns.message: The acceptance does not define "neighbouring islands", "longest useful crossing" or the path metric. The metric has to be integer: octile costs such as 5/7, because `Math.sqrt` is banned in content.
concerns.consequence: The validator can be written to pass vacuously, for example by picking the nearest pair only or measuring island centres instead of docks, and it would still 'fail on a broken map' in some trivial sense. Define it: dock-to-dock shortest sea paths at the content max-speed constant that the simulation also uses; each island's nearest other island is 20–40 s away; the maximum over all dock pairs and spawn-to-nearest-dock is ≤ 90 s; include negative tests (a moved island, a sealed dock).

concerns.message: Driving a ship with acceleration and turning from the keyboard in Playwright is timing-sensitive if the test is open-loop ("hold ArrowUp 1200 ms, ArrowLeft 300 ms"). The server steps at 20 Hz, held input expires after 250 ms, and the test fails when CI speed differs.
concerns.consequence: sail-and-dock and out-of-sight fail intermittently, and a single flaky run fails the browser check (retries: 0). Place the ship next to the shoal and dock with a known heading, and steer in a closed loop: each HUD entry exposes x, y, heading, speed and dock as data attributes, and the test waits on those authoritative values instead of wall-clock sleeps.

concerns.message: duel-core builds on the existing simulation modules (`hash.ts` `hashState`/`canonicalize`, `fixed.ts`, `random.ts`). This lane owns all of `packages/simulation/src` apart from `duel/` and may refactor them. `ShipSchema.heading` is also `t.uint8()`, so any heading resolution above 256 wraps silently.
concerns.consequence: Git merges the two branches cleanly, but the merged tree fails typecheck or the duel determinism tests if an export of these modules is renamed or its signature changes. Only add to fixed.ts, hash.ts and random.ts, never rename or change them. Keep headings at 256 or fewer, or widen the schema field.

simpler_alternative: Keep what decisions.md settles (Tiled source, one lane, StateView) and cut the moving parts around it. Size the world by lowering max ship speed (about 2–3 tiles/s) so the map stays near 100×80 tiles and can be read and authored as CSV. Keep the existing input shape: moveY for throttle/brake, moveX for turn, one `buttons` bit for interact. That leaves only the version number and a bit constant to change in the protocol. Put a public `playerCount` in MatchState and filter only the ships map. Make the test placement a per-match request that the env var unlocks, not a global spawn list. Put the converter core in content as a pure function with a thin fs wrapper in scripts/, and put the drift test under apps/server/src.
cheap_experiment: Before any map or sailing work, run a spike of about 30 minutes on the current skeleton. Tag the `ships` field as view-only in `apps/server/src/schema.ts` using @colyseus/schema 5.0.34's `schema()` builder (whatever its `.view()` or `view: true` equivalent is). In `onJoin`, set `client.view = new StateView()` and `view.add` only the client's own ShipSchema. Then write a two-HeadlessClient integration test that checks `b.room.state.ships.get(a.sessionId) === undefined`, calls `view.add(aShip)` on b's view and waits for it to decode, then calls `view.remove` and waits for it to vanish. Also check that `code`, `frame` and a new `playerCount` still arrive. This either confirms the filtering works with the builder API and reflection decoding, or triggers the task's Colyseus stop condition early, before hours of map and sailing work.
